sentences.en: Some students become fearful that if they participate in any demonstrations, they're going to face disciplinary action.
sentences.zh: 一些学生开始担心，如果他们参加任何示威活动，就会面临纪律处分。

sentences.en: So, fast forward now to April, when these student protesters learned that President Shafiq is headed to Washington for her congressional testimony.
sentences.zh: 现在快进到4月，当时这些学生抗议者得知沙菲克校长正前往华盛顿出席国会听证会。

sentences.en: It's at this moment that they set out to build their encampment.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，他们着手建立自己的营地。

sentences.en: — I think there was obviously a lot of intention in timing those two things.
sentences.zh: — 我想在时间选择上显然有很多刻意的考量。

sentences.en: I think it's sort of inherently a critique on a political pressure and this congressional pressure that we saw build up against, of course, Claudine Gay at Harvard
sentences.zh: 我认为这本质上是对政治压力的一种批评，以及我们在哈佛的克劳丁·盖伊身上看到的这种国会压力

sentences.en: and McGill at UPenn.
sentences.zh: 和宾夕法尼亚大学的麦吉尔。

sentences.en: So, I think a lot of students and faculty have been frustrated at this idea that there are not only powers at the university that are dictating what's happening,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为许多学生和教职员工一直对这种观点感到沮丧，即不仅有大学内部的势力在左右局势，

sentences.en: but there are perhaps external powers that are also guiding the way here in terms of what the university feels like it must do or has to do.
sentences.zh: 可能还有外部势力也在指导大学在必须做的事情或认为不得不做的事情上的做法。

sentences.en: And I think that timing was super crucial.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为时机极其关键。

sentences.en: Having the encampment happen on the Wednesday morning of the hearing was an incredible, in some senses, interesting strategy to direct eyes sort of to different places, right?
sentences.zh: 将抗议营地安排在听证会当周的周三上午，从某种意义上说，这是一种吸引人们视线投向不同地方的有趣策略，对吧？

sentences.en: All eyes were going to be on Shafiq in D.C., but now a lot of eyes are on New York.
sentences.zh: 所有的目光本将集中在华盛顿的沙菲克身上，但现在许多目光都转向了纽约。

sentences.en: The encampment is set up in the middle of the night, such morning, prior to the hearing.
sentences.zh: 抗议营地是在深夜搭建的，就在听证会当天的清晨。

sentences.en: And so what effectively happened is they caught Shafiq when she wasn't on campus, when a lot of senior administration had their resources dedicated to supporting Shafiq in D.C.
sentences.zh: 因此实际发生的情况是，他们抓住了沙菲克不在校园的机会，当时许多高级行政人员的资源都专门用来在华盛顿支持沙菲克。

sentences.en: And you have all of those people sort of not necessarily out of commission, but with their focus elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 而你们所有这些人可以说是并非丧失行动能力，但他们的注意力被转移到了其他地方。

sentences.en: So the encampment is met with very little resistance at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 因此，抗议营地在初期几乎没有遇到什么阻力。

sentences.en: There were sort of public safety officers floating around and sort of watching, but at the very beginning hours, I think there was a sense of, we did.
sentences.zh: 有一些公共安全人员在周围游荡并进行观察，但在最初的几个小时里，我想有一种“我们做到了”的感觉。

sentences.en: It would be quite surprising to anybody and an administrator to now suddenly see dozens of tents on this lawn in a way that I think very purposely
sentences.zh: 对于任何人以及行政人员来说，现在突然在这片草坪上看到几十个帐篷，会感到非常震惊，我认为这非常刻意地

sentences.en: puts an imagery of we're here to stay.
sentences.zh: 营造出一种“我们是来长久驻扎的”的视觉形象。

sentences.en: As the morning kind of evolved and congressional hearing continued,
sentences.zh: 随着清晨的发展和国会听证会的继续，

sentences.en: Then we started seeing university delegates that were coming to the encampment saying, you know, you may face disciplinary action for continuing to be here.
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始看到大学代表来到营地，说，你知道，如果你继续呆在这里，你可能会面临纪律处分。

sentences.en: I think that started around almost like 9 or 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我想那大约是在上午9点或10点左右。

sentences.en: They started handing out these code of conduct violation notices.
sentences.zh: 他们开始分发这些违反行为准则的通知。

sentences.en: Then there started to be more public safety sort of action and presence.
sentences.zh: 然后公共安全的行动和存在感开始增加。

sentences.en: So they started like barricading the entrances.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始像 barricading 一样封锁入口。

sentences.en: The day progressed, there was more threat of discipline.
sentences.zh: 随着一天的进展，纪律处分的威胁更大了。

sentences.en: The students became informed that if they continue to stay, they will face potential academic sanctions, potential suspension.
sentences.zh: 学生们被告知，如果他们继续留下来，将面临潜在的学术制裁和停学处分。

sentences.en: The more they try to silence us, the louder we will be.
sentences.zh: 他们越是试图让我们闭嘴，我们的声音就会越大。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people were like, okay, you're threatening us with suspension, but so what?
sentences.zh: 我想很多人当时的想法是，好吧，你们在用停学威胁我们，但那又怎样？

sentences.en: This is about the systems that Manoush Shafiq, that the board of trustees, that Columbia University is complicit in.
sentences.zh: 这关乎曼努什·沙菲克、董事会以及哥伦比亚大学所串通一气的这些体制。

sentences.en: What are you going to do to try to get us out of here?
sentences.zh: 你们打算怎么把我们弄出去？

sentences.zh: 而这显然很快就得到了回应。

sentences.en: This is the general police that the way of now is an unauthorized encampment.
sentences.zh: 这是总警局，目前的这条路是一处未经授权的营地。

sentences.en: We'll be arrested and charged with trespassing.
sentences.zh: 我们会被逮捕并被指控非法入侵。

sentences.en: My phone blew up, obviously, from the reporters, from the editors, of saying, oh my God, the NYPD is on our campus.
sentences.zh: 我的手机显然被打爆了，记者、编辑都在打，天哪，纽约警察局竟然来到了我们的校园。

sentences.en: And as soon as I saw that, I came out and I saw a huge crowd of students and affiliates on campus watching the lawns.
sentences.zh: 我一看到那个，就走出来，看到校园里有一大群学生和相关人员在围观草坪。

sentences.en: And as I kind of circled around that crowd, I saw the last end of the New York Police Department pulling away protesters and kind of clearing out the last of the encampment.
sentences.zh: 当我绕着那个人群走时，我看到纽约警察局的最后几个人正在拉走抗议者，并清理了营地的最后一部分。

sentences.en: We see you!

sentences.zh: 这真的是难以想象的事情。

sentences.en: Over a hundred students slash other individuals are arrested from our campus, forcefully removed.
sentences.zh: 有一百多名学生和其他个人从我们的校园被捕，被强行带走。

sentences.en: And although they were suspended, there was a feeling of, you know, this traumatic event that has just happened to these students, but also this sense of like,
sentences.zh: 尽管他们被停学了，但有一种感觉，你知道的，这些学生刚刚经历了这场创伤性事件，同时还有一种感觉，

sentences.en: okay, the worst of the worst that could have happened to us just happened.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对我们来说最糟糕的最糟糕的事情刚刚发生了。

sentences.en: And for those students who maybe couldn't go back to into campus, now all of their peers who were supporters or are in solidarity are in some senses further emboldened.
sentences.zh: 对于那些可能无法返回校园的学生来说，现在所有支持他们或声援他们的同龄人在某种意义上更加受到鼓舞了。

sentences.en: They're now not just sitting on the lawns for a pro-Palestinian cause, but also for the students who have endured quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 他们现在不仅是为了声援巴勒斯坦事业而坐在草坪上，也是为了那些经历了相当多苦难的学生。

sentences.en: So the crackdown sought by the president and enforced by the NYPD ends up, you're saying, becoming a galvanizing force for a broader group of Columbia students
sentences.zh: 所以，校长寻求、纽约警察局执行的镇压，最终成为了一股凝聚力，你的意思是，它团结了比最初

sentences.en: than were originally drawn to the idea of ever showing up on the center of campus and protesting.
sentences.zh: 被吸引到校园中心并参加抗议的想法所吸引的更广泛的哥伦比亚大学学生群体。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can certainly speak to the fact that
sentences.zh: 是的，我当然可以这样说，因为

sentences.en: I've seen my own peers, friends, or even acquaintances who weren't necessarily previously very involved in activism and organizing efforts.
sentences.zh: 我看到我自己的同龄人、朋友，甚至是以前不怎么参与激进主义和组织工作的熟人。

sentences.en: They're suddenly finding themselves involved.
sentences.zh: 他们突然发现自己卷入了其中。

sentences.zh: 我能问你一个问题吗，就是，

sentences.zh: 所有的新闻，

sentences.zh: 学生新闻，还是非学生新闻，都是历史的一种初稿。

sentences.en: And I wonder if we think of this as a historic moment for Columbia, how you imagine it's going to be remembered.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我们把这看作是哥伦比亚大学的一个历史性时刻，你觉得人们会如何记住它。

sentences.en: Yeah, there is no doubt in my mind that this will be a historic moment for Columbia.
sentences.zh: 是的，我毫不怀疑这将是哥伦比亚大学的一个历史性时刻。

sentences.en: I think that this will be remembered as a moment in which the fractures were laid bare.
sentences.zh: 我认为这将作为一个裂痕完全暴露出来的时刻而被人们记住。

sentences.en: Really, we got to see some of the disunity of the community in ways that I have never really seen it before.
sentences.zh: 真的，我们看到了一些社区的不团结，这种程度是我以前从未真正见过的。

sentences.en: And what we'll be looking to is where do we go from here?
sentences.zh: 我们要关注的是，接下来我们要去哪里？

sentences.en: How does Columbia repair?
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学如何修复？

sentences.en: How do we heal from all of this?
sentences.zh: 我们如何从这一切中恢复过来？

sentences.en: That is the big question in terms of what will happen.
sentences.zh: 关于未来会发生什么，这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: Nick,
sentences.zh: 尼克，

sentences.en: Isabella Ramirez just walked us through what this has all looked like from the perspective of a Columbia student.
sentences.zh: 伊莎贝拉·拉米雷斯刚刚带我们了解了从哥伦比亚大学学生的角度来看这一切的样子。

sentences.en: And from what she could tell, the crackdown ordered by President Shafiq did not quell much of anything.
sentences.zh: 据她所知，沙菲克校长下令的镇压并没有平息什么。

sentences.en: It seemed instead to really intensify everything on campus.
sentences.zh: 相反，它似乎让校园里的所有事情都真正加剧了。

sentences.en: I'm curious what this has looked like for Shafiq.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道这对沙菲克来说是什么样子的。

sentences.en: It's not just the students who are upset.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是学生们感到沮丧。

sentences.en: You have faculty including professors who are not necessarily sympathetic to the protesters' view of the war who are really outraged about what Shafiq has done here.
sentences.zh: 你还有教职员工，包括那些对抗议者的战争观不一定持同情态度的教授，他们对沙菲克在这里所做的事情感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: They feel that she's crossed a boundary that hasn't been crossed on Columbia's campus in a really long time.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得她越过了哥伦比亚大学校园里很久没有被越过的底线。

sentences.en: And so you start to hear things by the end of last week like censure, no confidence votes, questions about from her own professors about whether or not she can stay in power.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始在上周结束时听到一些事情，比如谴责、不信任投票、她自己的教授对她是否还能继续掌权的质疑。

sentences.en: So this creates a whole new front for her.
sentences.zh: 所以这为她开辟了一个全新战线。

sentences.en: And on top of it all, as this is going on, the encampment itself starts to reform tent by tent.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，当这一切正在发生时，营地本身开始帐篷连帐篷地重建。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Almost in the same place that it was.
sentences.zh: 几乎就在它原来的地方。

sentences.en: And Shafiq decides that the most important thing she could do is to try and take the temperature down, which means letting the encampment stand.
sentences.zh: 沙菲克认为她能做的最重要的事情就是试图降低热度，这意味着让营地继续存在。

sentences.en: Or in other words, leaning in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 或者换句话说，向另一个方向倾斜。

sentences.en: This time, we're going to let the protesters have their say for a little while longer.
sentences.zh: 这一次，我们要让抗议者再表达一会儿他们的意见。

sentences.en: The problem with that is that over the weekend, a series of images start to emerge from on campus and just off of it of some really troubling anti-Semitic episodes.
sentences.zh: 问题是，在周末，校园里和校园外开始出现一系列非常令人不安的反犹太主义事件的照片。

sentences.en: In one case, a guy holds up a poster in the middle of campus and points it towards a group of Jewish students who are counter-protesting.
sentences.zh: 在其中一个案例中，一个人在校园中央举着一张海报，指向一群正在进行反抗议的犹太学生。

sentences.en: And it says,

sentences.en: Hamas's next targets.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯的下一个目标。

sentences.zh: 我看到过一张那样的照片。

sentences.en: those Jewish students.
sentences.zh: 那些犹太学生。

sentences.zh: 这是一个非常直接且刺耳的声明。

sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学紧闭的大门外，

sentences.en: protesters are showing up from across New York City.
sentences.zh: 来自纽约市各地的抗议者纷纷赶来。

sentences.en: It's hard to tell who's affiliated with Colombia, who's not.
sentences.zh: 很难分清谁是哥伦比亚大学的，谁不是。

sentences.en: There's a video that goes viral of one of them shouting at Jewish students, go back to Poland, go back to Europe.
sentences.zh: 有一段视频在网上疯传，其中一人对犹太学生大喊，回波兰去，回欧洲去。

sentences.en: In other words, a clear message, you're not welcome here.

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 这并不代表营地中绝大多数一直以来都保持和平的抗议者。

sentences.en: They would later hold a Seder, actually, with some of the pro-Palestinian Jewish protesters in their ranks.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们后来与队伍中的一些亲巴勒斯坦的犹太抗议者举行了逾越节晚餐。

sentences.en: But those videos are reaching members of Congress, the very same Republicans that Shafiq had testified in front of just a few days before.
sentences.zh: 但这些视频传到了国会议员那里，也就是几天前沙菲克刚向其作证的那些共和党人那里。

sentences.en: And now, they're looking and saying, you have lost control of your campus, you've turned back on your word to us, and you need to resign.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们看着并说，你已经失去了对校园的控制，你违背了对我们的承诺，你需要辞职。

sentences.en: They call for her outright resignation over this.
sentences.zh: 他们为此直接呼吁她辞职。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Shafiq's dilemma here is pretty extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 所以沙菲克在这里的困境非常非同寻常。

sentences.zh: 进一步疏远和激怒那些对第一次镇压仍然非常生气的学生和教职员工。

sentences.en: And now, both ends of this spectrum, lawmakers in Washington, folks on the Columbia campus, are saying she can't lead the university over this situation before she's even made any
sentences.zh: 现在，这个光谱的两端，华盛顿的议员们、哥伦比亚大学的人们，都在说她不能因为这种情况而领导这所大学，甚至在她做出任何

sentences.zh: 关于如何处理这第二个营地的决定之前。

sentences.en: No.
